en.headline: Police find insufficient evidence to charge basketball coach over student video
en.dek: Yung Kam-wah, a former Hong Kong national team player and Basketball Association vice-chairman, will not face prosecution after an investigation into a viral clip from a school training session.
body: Police said on Friday there was insufficient evidence to charge anyone over a video that showed a basketball coach forcing a secondary school student to slap himself.

The decision follows an in-depth investigation into the clip, which surfaced earlier this year and was recorded during the 2023-24 academic year at Hon Wah College in Siu Sai Wan. Yung Kam-wah, 54, a former Hong Kong men’s national team player, current vice-chairman of the Basketball Association of Hong Kong, China, and sports commentator, had been arrested in early June on suspicion of common assault and released on bail.

The school had suspended Yung from coaching duties and reported the matter to police. Yung earlier posted a public apology acknowledging the incident. Police notified the relevant parties of the outcome.
No charges will be laid against any person in connection with the case.

zh.headline: 籃球教練迫學生掌摑案 警方指證據不足不檢控
zh.dek: 前港隊球員、籃總副主席翁金華涉校內訓練片段，警方完成深入調查後表示證據不足以起訴任何人。
body: 警方星期五表示，經深入調查後，認為一宗涉及籃球教練強迫中學生掌摑自己的影片，證據不足以起訴任何人。
片段於本年較早時在網上流傳，拍攝於2023至24學年小西灣漢華中學訓練期間。54歲翁金華是前香港男子籃球代表隊球員、現任中國香港籃球總會副主席及體育評述員，他於6月初涉嫌普通襲擊被捕，其後獲准保釋。
學校早前已暫停翁金華的教練職務，並向警方報案。翁金華其後在社交平台公開道歉，承認事件。警方已將結果通知相關人士。
案件不會有任何人被起訴。
